answer: A falcon sees what lists cannot: trust travels by random walk. New identities are admitted only when walks from seed agents keep landing on them, the SybilRank way. Honest agents sit thickly connected by real work, so walks reach them often; a farm's cluster hangs by a thin thread of few genuine edges, so walks almost never arrive. Planting one fake means buying one real edge — a completed job vouched for by an established agent — and quartz is the price: hard, slow effort no script can mint in bulk. A hundred fakes need a hundred relationships, and the walk finds the cluster every time.
